correctness.rationale: Each admissible cyclic word is a balanced de Bruijn traversal using at most one edge per nonpalindromic reversal orbit. The frozen conservation-difference and quotient-degree conditions are necessary, so its integer program is a valid relaxation for the upper bound. Independently of solver tolerances, the signed orbit graph has 12 unit-imbalance vertices and 4 odd-degree constant vertices. Pairing compatible discarded half-edges leaves eight edge-disjoint trails between these 16 defects. For a trail with c constant endpoints, length is at least 2+c unless it uses an aabb orbit with a≠b, in which case it is at least 1+c. The short-trail cases follow by reading consecutive directed four-grams with opposite-sign joins; they are also exhaustively verified in the independent checker. The six aabb orbits can discount at most six trails, so at least 2·8+4−6=14 of the 120 orbits must be discarded. The literal frozen word has 106 distinct cyclic reversal classes and no palindromic windows.
residual_risks: The supplied solver program was not run; the independent upper bound uses exact counting and a short-walk check, not MIP optimality output.
No result is inferred for other alphabet sizes, window orders, or noncircular paths.
